original_question: Find the asymptotic value of phi(n,4,4), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set in which every four-point subset determines at least four distinct distances; equivalently, the set contains no rhombus, no rectangle, and no deltoid with one vertex equidistant from the other three.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 29 (renumbered as Section 7, Problem 30 in later revisions): find the asymptotic value of φ(n,4,4).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct target quantity φ(n,4,4), the correct local condition that every 4-point subset determines at least 4 distinct distances, the planar setting, and the paper’s nearby forbidden-configuration reformulation in terms of rhombuses, rectangles, and a deltoid with one vertex equidistant from the other three.
missing_details: The ambient space should be stated explicitly as the Euclidean plane R^2.
φ(n,4,4) should be defined formally as a minimum over all finite sets P⊂R^2 of n distinct points satisfying the local condition.
The phrase 'determines at least four distinct distances' should be made explicit as referring to the six pairwise Euclidean distances among any 4-point subset.

If the forbidden-pattern reformulation is used, the paper’s standing convention in this part of the section is that degenerate polygons are also included; this affects the exact meaning of the equivalence.
The question should state that the goal is the asymptotic order of growth as n→∞.
refined_question: Let φ(n,4,4) be the minimum possible cardinality of the distance set {|pq| : p,q∈P, p≠q} over all sets P⊂R^2 of n distinct points such that every 4-point subset Q⊂P determines at least 4 distinct pairwise Euclidean distances among its 6 interpoint distances. Determine the asymptotic order of growth of φ(n,4,4) as n→∞.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, using the paper’s convention that degenerate polygons are also counted in this part of the discussion, determine the asymptotic minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point set P⊂R^2 that contains no 4-point subset forming a rhombus, a rectangle, or a deltoid with one vertex equidistant from the other three.
justification: The draft is very close to the paper’s actual open problem. Section 6 first defines φ(n,k,l) for planar point sets, Table 3 lists the specific row for φ(n,4,4), and the paragraph immediately before Problem 29 gives the exact forbidden-configuration interpretation for φ(n,4,4). The paper’s official formulation itself is simply 'Find the asymptotic value of φ(n,4,4),' so the main refinements needed are to make the minimization, the Euclidean-plane setting, the 6 pairwise distances in each 4-subset, and the degenerate-polygon convention explicit.
